themes_detail.label: Dead Animal Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Park Slope/Carroll Gardens experienced 8 dead animal complaints THIS WEEK, a 967% spike compared to the 0.8 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 10.96), suggesting a sudden public health or environmental event requiring urgent investigation.
evidence: 8 dead animal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly baseline (967% increase)
Z-score of 10.96 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Spike appeared in current week data only, suggesting acute event
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Dept and NYC Health about what's driving the sudden spike—disease outbreak, poisoning, or environmental contamination?
Canvass affected streets (focus on Carroll Gardens and Park Slope proper) to document locations and resident concerns
Investigate whether this correlates with any known ecological or pest control incidents in adjacent areas

themes_detail.label: Damaged Trees Surge
themes_detail.summary: Damaged tree complaints hit 13 THIS WEEK, a 395% spike from the 2.6 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.58), concentrated in a neighborhood where Parks capital budget requests repeatedly cite park infrastructure upgrades.
evidence: 13 damaged tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.6 weekly baseline (395% increase)
Z-score of 6.58 indicates strong statistical significance
Community Board has repeatedly requested park infrastructure upgrades and tree maintenance funding
Damage tree complaints rank #9 overall in 90-day volume (304 total), suggesting systemic issue
reporting_angles: Interview NYC Parks about storm damage, disease, or maintenance backlog affecting trees across the district
Map this week's complaints geographically to identify if damage is concentrated in specific parks or streets
Connect to long-standing Community Board requests for park infrastructure—is this the crisis that finally triggers funding?

themes_detail.label: Graffiti and Illegal Dumping Escalation
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints jumped to 15 LAST WEEK, a 314% spike from the 3.6 weekly average, while illegal dumping complaints hit 22 LAST WEEK (175% above the 8-week average of 8.0), suggesting coordinated environmental decay or gang activity.
evidence: 15 graffiti complaints LAST WEEK vs. 3.6 weekly baseline (314% increase, z-score: 5.89)
22 illegal dumping complaints LAST WEEK vs. 8.0 weekly baseline (175% increase, z-score: 5.49)
Both spikes appeared in the same reporting window, suggesting possible connected phenomenon
Illegal dumping is 275% above baseline; coupled with graffiti, indicates neighborhood disorder escalation
reporting_angles: Investigate whether graffiti and dumping are concentrated in same neighborhoods or blocks—potential gang territory marking or organized dumping operation
Interview NYPD, Sanitation, and local precinct about enforcement activity and whether they've noticed uptick
Check if construction or development (1,014 DOB permits filed in 90 days) is creating dumping opportunities or attracting illegal activity

themes_detail.label: Bike Infrastructure Complaints Explode
themes_detail.summary: Bike Rack complaints surged to 5 THIS WEEK (1233% above the 0.4 weekly average, z-score: 9.55) and Abandoned Bike complaints hit 5 LAST WEEK (700% above the 0.6 baseline, z-score: 6.29), suggesting rapid deterioration of bike infrastructure or oversight.
evidence: 5 bike rack complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (1233% increase, z-score: 9.55)
5 abandoned bike complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly baseline (700% increase, z-score: 6.29)
Combined signal across two related complaint types suggests systemic bike infrastructure issue
Both metrics are near-zero baseline, so raw numbers are small but statistical anomaly is extreme
reporting_angles: Contact NYC DOT to understand what's driving sudden spike in bike rack failures and abandoned bikes
Investigate whether bikes are being removed during construction or development activity; cross-reference with 1,014 DOB permits filed
Interview bike advocacy groups in Park Slope/Carroll Gardens about condition of local infrastructure and whether this reflects broader neglect

themes_detail.label: Wood Pile Dumping Problem
themes_detail.summary: Wood pile complaints hit 3 LAST WEEK, a 2300% spike from the 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 8.69), indicating illegal dumping or construction debris accumulation that may relate to the 36 demolitions and 1,014 total DOB permits filed.
evidence: 3 wood pile complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (2300% increase, z-score: 8.69)
36 full demolitions filed in 90-day DOB data; 641 alterations also filed
Wood pile spike temporally adjacent to illegal dumping spike (both last week), suggesting construction-related debris problem
Extremely low baseline (0.1 per week) means even small absolute number reflects major statistical anomaly
reporting_angles: Investigate whether wood piles are debris from the 36 active demolitions or from illegal dumping operations
Interview Department of Sanitation and DOB about enforcement of construction debris regulations in the district
Map wood pile complaints against active construction sites to determine if there's a geographic correlation
